utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. No one on -- well, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Is there anything you want to bring to our attention?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We have an excellent piece of news, is that the communication between the Prosecution and the Defence is progressing. And yesterday, we had some success, and that's the first point. And I believe everyone will be satisfied. The second point is that Defence cannot work at all on the basis of the documents given by the Prosecution because there is a number of exhibits that we were given yesterday for a crucial witness that we should hear next week. And I think I can give these documents that were copied, copied yesterday. Now, what we were given by the Prosecution, such things, and we took them a little randomly. But exhibits are completely illegible, and I think these are photographs, or perhaps it's modern art, but we cannot use them at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you give us examples that you have prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we would like is that we can have some legible documents; otherwise, we cannot work. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I asked to have copies in front of me. I don't know whether the copying by the Defence deteriorated in any way the quality of what has been provided to the Defence. But if it really would be true that the Defence is provided with copies like these, could you then give us an explanation as to what -- I don't know whether... Could you respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'll make some inquiries during the morning and update the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps immediately following one of the two breaks that we'll have during the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because if this has been distributed, you must have some people on your team who are blind or -- I mean, you can't really. So that's -- this doesn't need any further explanation. Please inform us as soon as you can. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'll return this. I mean, this was just for our information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. This was just to show that we have the original, and at a distance, even a blind person could see that we cannot see anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I also now see that these are parts of longer documents, of which other parts might be legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I said, but this is what I wanted everyone to see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Anything else? Well, then at least I was very happy with your first remark. Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the witness because, Mr. Ierace, I think we are ready to proceed with the examination-in-chief of Fajko Kadric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kadric. May I remind you that you are still bound today by the solemn declaration you made yesterday, that you tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Mr. Ierace will continue to examine you. Please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At this stage, I ask that the video, which is Exhibit number P3279N be displayed -- excuse me, Mr. President, P3280N is the correct exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, Mr. Usher, would you please verify that the witness is -- yes. Is there any problem in playing the video or should I just be more patient? Yes, there we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "INVESTIGATOR: Please face in the direction [Indiscernible] you were driving, to the best of your recollection, on the morning of the day that your son was wounded. Could you please indicate with your hand on which side of your vehicle you heard the bullet impact, to the best of your recollection, when your son was wounded. Could you please stand in the location where you recall, to the best of your recollection, the end of the sniping barricades was located on that day. I am now going to mark that location with yellow spray paint. Will you now please stand at the location where, to the best of your recollection, you were located as the driver of your vehicle at the time that your son was wounded? I will now mark that location with yellow spray paint and the figure 'X'."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We saw and heard that the investigator asked you to indicate certain positions at the intersection and certain directions. When you complied with those directions, did you do so truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, I'd like the 360-degree photograph to be displayed, that is Exhibit P3279N. My case manager will assist us with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, do you recognise the image which appears on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the street which appears to the left on the screen the street along which you were driving at the time that your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please navigate the image slowly to the right. Please pause there. Do we now see the intersection which was in the area where your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the centre of the picture is a white building, of approximately ten storeys. Do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. Yes. It is a student residences.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. When watching the video, we saw you indicate a position on the roadway which marked one end of a barricade. Do you see on this image where that position was marked by the investigator with a line of yellow spray paint?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that appear on the pedestrian crossing, which is marked with white stripes across the intersection?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a very clear picture, but I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is the mark -- if I can put it to you this way: Is the mark on the white --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes -- Mr. Usher, could you please -- it depends on what button is pushed. I see the quality is quite different. If, for example, you push the button for video, you have a rather bad picture, and if you put on the computer evidence, you have, as far as I can see, the better picture. Could you please see that the witness has the best possible picture in front of him. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you now able to see the yellow paint line that was marked in your direction, indicating the end of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, do I understand that the quality of the picture is not as it is on the other screens? Madam Registrar, could this be fixed because I see that the quality on the different screens is quite distinctive. If this cannot be fixed, I'll have to ask the witness to look at another screen. I see there's quite a difference in quality of the picture, and the witness should have the best. Please, if you... It's confirmed by the technician that the picture on the screen for the witness is similar to what it is for me, and I think that's clear enough to work with. So, Mr. Ierace, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. This is just for the transcript. I don't know whether it is important to mention because it doesn't seem very obvious. We have a problem of looking at various images on the screen -- screens, and I believe that this photograph, 360-degree photographs, can bring in more confusion than clarity. That is the reason why I would like to stress it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the quality of your computer screen as such is not good enough, we'll check that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. But as you know, we decided that the 360-degrees photographs were rather helping the Court than confusing the Court. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, are you now able to see on the image in front of you the yellow mark made at your direction indicating the end of the barricades?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see a yellow line where I marked, but I can tell that this is the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Are you able to -- could you please tell us where the barricade -- withdraw that. Could you please tell us where the end of the barricades was if it appears in the picture in front of you? Please do not point at the screen because we cannot see where you are pointing. Rather, could you describe to us where it was.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, if we look at this blue car, straight there, in front of that blue car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Please continue to -- can you tell us, what was the nature of the barricade? What was it made from?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were concrete blocks, concrete slabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How high were they?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How high were the concrete blocks?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the barricade extend right across the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is -- since the interpreter didn't hear it, perhaps for the transcript, we could repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was translated, the answer. "Approximately 2 metres high."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the barricade extend right across the road which now appears in the image, being Aleja Branka Bujica?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript, the view which is on the screen at the moment shows the 10-storey building previously identified by the witness to the left, and a similar building to the right. And in the middle of the image, what appears to be a house with approximately three storeys with a red roof.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, the building on the right, that is, the 10-storey building on the right, what is the present use of that building?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The United Nations are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the 10-storey building on the left which you earlier identified, what was its condition during the war, and in particular, on the day that your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were completely hollow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that one was able to see the floors from one end to the other?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In relation to the 3-storey building with the red roof in the middle of the picture, what was the condition of that building during the conflict, and in particular, on the day your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had two floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your earlier evidence, we now see in the centre of the screen the street up which you were driving at the time your son was shot.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan to the right. Please pause there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I take it we now see the direction in which you were headed at the time your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that the bullet entry point was on the passenger side of the cabin, that is, to your right. Was it possible from the position where your son was shot to see any buildings on the Serb army side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will continue to pan slowly to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And if you see those positions, will you please say so, and we will stop the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please pan slowly to the right.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stop. I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, the centre of the image at the moment is a blue -- approximately, is a blue rubbish tin or garbage bin and alongside it is a white --

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- is a whitish utility box. Now, where is that position in relation to the blue garbage bin? Is it above it, to the left of it, to the right of it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, up across the tree -- above the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Excuse me, Mr. President. I'll ask that we now zoom in on that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We have now zoomed in on the approximate area that you indicated. Can you describe to us where that position or those positions were, having regard to the image?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right next to the trees over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think we see a tree growing on a grassy strip, slightly to the right of the garbage bin. Were the positions behind that tree, to the left of that tree, or to the right of that tree?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that part here but slightly higher up. They were on an upper floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Upper floor of what building?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first floor, the first floor. There is the ground floor and then the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the name of that building?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The home for the blind, Dom Slijepih.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage I'd ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3277. It's a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, do you recognise the photograph which has been placed to your right? Rather than -- rather than look at it on the computer screen, could you turn your body and look at the actual photograph to your right? Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please adjust one of the microphones so that the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does it show the same intersection? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you make a statement on the 28th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time you made your statement, did you place some blue marks on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you place some markings on the intersection, on the roadway itself, indicating the position of the barrier?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did you also place some marks -- I'll withdraw that. Are you able to see on this photograph the position of the home for the blind?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I think if you use the pointer to indicate the tree, which we earlier discussed on the 360-degree photograph, that is a tree which appears to be on the grass verge and has a blue line ruled across towards the top of it. There are two such trees. This is the tree to the left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, do I understand you to mean that the building was behind that tree?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time your son was shot, was that tree present?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was smaller, much smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time your son was shot, and from the position your son was shot, were you able to see the home for the blind?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that moment, I wasn't really looking whether I could see it or not. I was driving. I wasn't looking for where it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you driven through that intersection before that day that your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that day, but yes, I did, on the days before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How often, in the months before your son was shot, would you drive through that intersection?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At times three times, at times five. It depended on the number of vehicles required to go into the centre and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the home for the blind have any particular significance for you on those occasions that you drove through that intersection?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was always a danger that -- a risk that we might be hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the home for the blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you been fired at on previous occasions that you had driven through that intersection?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had your vehicle been hit on previous occasions when you had driven through that intersection?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On what side of your vehicle -- withdraw that. From what side of the road had that fire come?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that the same side as it came from on the day that your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the same side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On those earlier occasions that you had driven through the intersection, had you ever noticed whether you could see the home for the blind?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a hole, a hole on the first floor. It was made in the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to see that from the intersection?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly at the place where we were hit, some ten metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From the intersection, could you see the hole in the wall of the home for the blind?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, as you drove up that hill towards the intersection, were you able to see the home for the blind through the exposed floors of the ten-storey building which appears on the right of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3279NN, which comprises two photographs. Please place the one with the number 11 on the ELMO first. Yes, that's it, I think. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, do you recognise the view in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to determine from that view where the photograph was taken from?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts is that?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here. That's where this building was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "here", where do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The home for the blind. This is the part of the home for the blind. This building did not exist there. I mean, it was destroyed, and this one was built later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Was the home for the blind one building or more than one building?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to determine where the photographer was at the time that he or she took this photograph by looking at the view of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. Here, in this building, the home to the blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, are you able to see in the photograph any part of the intersection -- withdraw that. You said the building to the bottom left, that is, with the black and orange and red roof, was not there at the time. Is that correct? I think you said it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, would you please look at the roof line of that building, that is, the roof which is black, red, and orange striped. And do you see above that roof line there appear to be some light poles, some grass, and part of a road?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness now be shown the second photograph of P3279NN.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you now see what appears to be a telephoto shot taken from the same position showing that detail?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the intersection which appears towards the centre of that photograph?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What intersection is it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one where we were hit, right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please come back to the other photograph, that is, the one with the "11." And firstly, looking at the same area of photograph 11, would you then move your eye to the left. And do you see what appears to be a portion of a building of around ten storeys? Perhaps you could point to that building when you think you have located it.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "building"? You mean the residential, the apartment block? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please move the pointer to the left, to the margin of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Further up. Just above the roof.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's it. Do you see there, there appears to be a building of approximately ten storeys with white and reddish brown horizontal stripes? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the student hostel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Those photographs might be returned now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You referred yesterday to your truck having a tank or a cistern in the back. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you carted water in that cistern, where did you collect it from?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to Halilovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you delivered -- where did you deliver the water to?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which particular locality?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojnicko Polje, or Saraj Polje as it's called now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that also the area in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who would use the water?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the residents there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How would they collect the water from the tank?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a faucet and a hose, and they would come with cannisters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the capacity of the tank?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 3.000 litres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you were transporting water, how frequently would you take a load to that settlement?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At times, three times; at times, two times; and at times, five times. It varied.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were they times per day, per week, per month, or what?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Per day, per day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You said that on this day, you were transporting flour. Who was to receive the flour?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the neighbourhood community, that is, Civil Defence rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How was the flour to be distributed?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was paid for in 1992. The civilians had paid for it but did not get it before that. And now it had arrived, so they simply collected what they had paid for.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One aspect I've overlooked. Perhaps I could...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown the map which is P3108. The witness was shown this map yesterday, and therefore copies have already been distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, it has not yet been admitted into evidence, so it should -- we usually do that at the end of the examination of the witnesses, after he has been cross-examined. So it should still be... But I have a copy here, if the parties would agree, just for -- it's 3108, is it, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You found it, yes. Perhaps then we use the original one, and since there will be some markings on it. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the left-hand side of the map could be placed on the ELMO. I'm not sure if that's the correct map. Mr. President, could we check the exhibit number of that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. That's not the correct one. What we need is -- it's 3108 with some handwriting in the left-hand corner. If you give that one to me -- yes, thank you. Just for the clarity of the transcript, could we please zoom in first on the exhibit number, since there has been some confusion, which is in the right, upper corner? Yes, first have that. I read 3108, yes. And now please zoom in at the left part of the -- yes. Please zoom in, a bit more to the left, I suggest. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Kadric, you explained the significance of the cross at the intersection and the arrows leading to the cross. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You also placed a blue circle around some buildings which appear to the left of the cross and slightly down. Do you see that blue circle?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you just pointed to them. What buildings were they?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is where the home for the blind is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You also placed a blue line along a street to the east, in particular, to the southeast of those buildings along a street. What is the significance of that line? Perhaps you could point to it as you give your explanation.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, you mean? This here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you moved the pointer down and to the right, you will see a blue line extending from the circle down a street -- yes.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You're on the line now. Could you move the pointer down rather than across?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. Do you see that there is a blue pen line going -- yes?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, this here? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the significance of that line that you placed on the map?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is Lukavicka Cesta. That is the name of the street where the demarcation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By "demarcation," do you mean the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please return the map to the Registrar. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you're ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very happy to do so, if the Chamber allows me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, now counsel for the Defence will examine you. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good morning. Will you please tell us if you made and did you make any written statements for the representatives of the Tribunal and, if so, if yes, when?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you make only one statement?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I went there once.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'd really like to ask you to tell me the truth. Don't you know how many statements you made?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did it in 1995, twice, in UN homes, and then there was this photographing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And you gave no other statements than that one of 1995? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, there were other statements too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, then, Witness, will you tell us all about it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, is it that you did not make any other statements apart from the one in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... that on line 18 of page 21, the witness said that there were other statements too, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I was asking for the date, Mr. President, if I may.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking this question simply because we have a date which is the 20th of September --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but your question was, "Is it that you did not make any other statements apart from the one in 1995?" When the witness just had testified that there were other statements. This question seems totally useless to me. If you want to know the dates, please proceed in such a way that you find out what the dates were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly, Mr. President. But my first question was when was the statement given, exactly on what dates, so I am going to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you confirm that it was in the year 2001? Because what we have is a different date. So is it 2000, 2001, for your very last declaration -- for your very last statement?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was born in 1949, not -- that's not when I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But what I wanted to know is when did you give the statement? Was it 2000 or 2001? This is just to clarify the question. That's where the problem lies. Is it in 2000 or is it in 2001 that you gave your last statement?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember but I went twice to Nedzarici, to the UN centre. I went there twice, but I don't know what the dates were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. President, I would like to submit 02114297 because the witness is not sure are we talking about 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that you gave a statement in 1995, that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately six years ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you also give a statement last summer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, thank you for your answer. You were a soldier throughout the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Until the wounding, I was a soldier, and then I was no longer a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. Until the moment of the incident you're talking about, the wounding, you're talking about until the incident, you were a soldier?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, what was your rank, if you had one?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you belong to the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Where were you stationed?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Where exactly, address and number, please?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the square of the 10th Krajina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you have a slightly more precise indication? Was there a number of the street?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven, number seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. So you were stationed there. How many people were there? What was the strength?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2000 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: 2000 people. That's what I understand.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military, as well as civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I was asking about the brigade. And what I mean by "brigade," that means it's a military formation. And you just told me that there was civilians in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade was in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. You just told me, Witness, to my question when I asked you about where you were stationed, you gave me a precise -- precise address. That was number 7 of a square --

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you just wait until I finish my question. You told me that this is where you lived.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I believe -- what I was asking, I believe, I was precise. Where were you stationed? Where were you stationed as a military?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vojnicko Polje. Not in the barracks, in buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you were a soldier? You were in a unit, so you were somewhere where -- you went somewhere where you were called for your duty?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would go to my guard post duty for the first two months where I was supposed to stand guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. We are going to make questions more precise because I'm not getting any precise answers. Where was your guard post?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In number 7 of 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, let me just ask you a few questions. You said you were in the military, and you were talking about the beginning of the wartime.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where was your commander who would tell you where to go on guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The brigade was in Dobrinja, but one small company was in Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said the brigade was in Dobrinja. Could you tell us exactly where the brigade was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the street, but it was in the centre of Dobrinja, in Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you were on duty, who would tell you where to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or did you decide yourself where to go on guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first, we did it ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And later, a kind of company arrived. And there was a commander, and then they assigned duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where was this commander located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There, in the buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In what buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. It was number 9 or number 7 or number 11. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that the place where you lived, in those same buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the ground floor. So in the same building but not in your apartment but on the ground floor of the building --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am aware that I'm in a different position, but the tone you use while questioning might put the witness better at ease so that you get the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] You mean it's not charming enough?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to be charming to a witness. I'm just telling you that the tone might help you to get where you want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will make sure, Mr. President, to have a satisfactory tone of voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if I understood you correctly, there was a military station at the address where you lived and that you told us about a minute ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm going to have to change my tone again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But you just told us that where you lived, there was a military unit; there were troops. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 7 where this entrance, number 9 where this entrance, number 11, and number 13. So we went from number 7 to number 13. These were entrances. And number 9, there was business premises, and that's where it was. So it was number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, so you will agree with me that very near where you lived, there was one or several military stations, military posts?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one command, not several.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, if there is a command post, naturally there are troops, there are soldiers. Were there troops, soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were all civilians. There were no soldiers. They were not in uniform. They were, I suppose, soldiers but they did not wear uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So I understand at the command post, there were civilians?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I did not ask you if they were wearing uniforms. In spite of my tone, I was asking you whether you know that there were civilians at the command posts.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians were all in buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But what I thought I understood was that these civilian buildings, there were military installations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So that's a correct one. Very well. Now, in these civilian buildings, were there soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see that when I change the tone, it's going much better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... from reminding me that I made a certain remark about your behaviour in this courtroom. Would you please refrain from that. It's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not do it any more. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever I am talking, you find it necessary to remind me five, six, seven times a day that I said something to you. I'll not allow that any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, will not do it. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, how many soldiers were there, as far as you know, in this building or in these civilian buildings?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: About 50. And they were located in one or several civilian buildings?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to sleep. And then in the morning they would go to be called, the roll called, that's all. And they went to their duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. But they were called in one or several buildings, civilian buildings?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were called to one building where the command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. However, you just said that they slept at home. So there were no barracks that the soldiers could go to spend the night. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Sir, you were a soldier for a number of months. And could you tell me what weapons the soldiers had who were in these civilian buildings?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic rifles, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you not have any more important weapons, weapons that we call bazookas, anti-tank weapons?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they had nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, as far as you as a soldier, did you see any areas with trenches in your area of military activity?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was hard to see that, where the trenches were. If you try to look, you'd get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You yourself, you were never on duty in these trenches or anywhere near the trenches?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were at the entrance to the building, on anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were there soldiers in trenches or near trenches?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw them but whoever came close would get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I understand, Witness, but as far as you know, I am asking you as far as you know, when you were a soldier for several long months, do you know, yes or no, these trenches had soldiers in?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at guard duty for two months, and after that, I was no longer on duty. I simply drove a vehicle, and I don't know anything about trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you just said that you were just driving a vehicle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: While were you a soldier?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Corsa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You mean Corsa is very rarely used by an army?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Opel Corsa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was it a military vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you were driving -- as a soldier, you were driving a civilian vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. This Corsa vehicle, did it look like a small van?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was a passenger car.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness please break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you're telling me that as a soldier, you were driving a military --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, you may not have heard it, but the interpreting booth just requested that there be breaks between counsel's questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. Thank you to my colleague from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So I believe that I heard your answer, sir. You said yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What happens is what happens now and then, that is that it goes too quick, and I do know that you can hear the answer in the original language, so would you please slow down. I also will ask the witness. Mr. Kadric, would you please look at your screen. Wait until the text stops moving and then answer the question. Otherwise, the interpreters -- yes, perhaps you could change it to text. As soon as it stops moving, would you then please answer the question, since otherwise the interpreters are not able to follow you. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ierace, for your observation. Thank you, Mr. President. I will try and slow down a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, Witness, I believe that I understand you said yes, so that's correct, as a soldier, you were driving a civilian vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, as a soldier, did you wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, during your period of military service, did you ever receive a uniform?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what was the duration or the length of your daily service, daily duty, while you were in the army?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you were -- throughout the day, you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, without any exceptions?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "without exceptions"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, yes. Perhaps you had some days when you went home?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went home after I was -- I couldn't go home because I was driven out of Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, while you were driving the truck that you made a sketch of, were you on duty then?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was on duty. That was my work, civilian work. I did more for the civilians than I did for the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, my question was to find out whether you were on duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question was not quite clear because it depended on what kind of function, and I think the witness answered that question perfectly well. He said he was in function, and then he explained that he did more civilian work than military work. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you, as a soldier, did you have any insignia, any distinctive insignia, that could identify you as such?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Did you have a weapon, a personal weapon, that you had on you?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to have some localities indicated on the map, but first of all, I would like to cover as much questions as we could to gain time. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, bottom line, so no confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like us to now go back to the incident. And you said a moment ago that the shots came from the institute for the blind and you pointed to the first floor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, but you yourself did not see the shot? You did not see the actual shot as such?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't see it because we were driving.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. You also said that as far as you knew, there were positions on the ground floor, firing positions on the ground floor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "ground floor."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But Witness, you answered a Prosecution question in relation to the building, the institute for the blind, as the question was referring to the front line, the actual separation line between the two parties. Could you please confirm that this was the case, that the location where you were at the time of the incident was extremely near the front line, in the immediate vicinity of the front line?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Could you indicate approximately, as much as you can recall, what was the distance between you and the front line?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was about 200 metres, but many years have passed and, of course, the war has ended, and I never took the trouble of measuring that distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Now, Witness, I would like to go back to some other elements of the cross-examination. You said at the very beginning of your testimony yesterday that you had lived in Pale; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I believe that you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, about half a dozen questions back, my friend said -- this is page 33, line 12, on the English transcript, "You also said that as far as you knew, there were positions on the ground floor, firing positions on the ground floor; is that correct?" Answer: "I don't know what you mean by 'ground floor.'" I take it my friend was referring to testimony by the witness about firing positions in this school for the blind during examination-in-chief. I think that appears on page 11 at line 6, and in fact the evidence of the witness is that it was from the first floor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, when I was not attentive, it was because I was just checking because it was not my recollection. I've got it now. It's page 11, line 6. After having given the answer: "Well, at that part here, but slightly higher up. They were on an upper floor." And the question was: "Upper floor of what building?" And then the answer was: "The first floor, the first floor. There was the ground floor and then the first floor." So the objection is sustained, although the question has already been answered. And I may urge you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to be quite precise in quoting, because if I ask you to find the line, you are implicitly criticising me for wasting time. And if I do not urge you -- if you're not referring to a specific line, I have to establish that you are not very precise in your quoting. So what I'll do is, as long as you are precise in quoting, I'll not ask you at every occasion to indicate the exact line. If you continue misquoting, then unfortunately, I'll have to give you an order that you always specify exactly the source of your quotation. So it's up to you either to become more precise or to be forced by me to do so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. But I never, never would criticise this Chamber in any case, but thank you for your remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the tone sometimes again, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said - and if it is necessary, I will find the quote - but you said that you had been in -- you lived in Pale, and that you arrived in Sarajevo. And I think I can recall that you said that you had been driven away from Pale. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, when you say "driven away," could you perhaps be more precise and tell us who drove you away?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly I was driven away by the army, by the Yugoslav army and Karadzic's and Mladic's soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for this answer. You said that you then arrived in Sarajevo after a while, that you lived with your relatives, with your sister, then your sister-in-law. And I believe that you said that you changed your apartment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived in Breka, and I stayed a night in Breka, and then the next night I went to Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my question was the following: I believe you went to the sister, sister-in-law, and that you changed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're confusing things. I went to my sister's on just that day when you arrived from Vasin Han. From up there, we stayed a night in Breka, and we then went to Vojnicko Polje the next day, to my wife's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So you went to your sister's, and then to your sister-in-law's, and then you changed your apartment, that you went elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He lived in number 13, on the first floor. And I went to live in number 7 on the seventh floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you took another apartment, Witness, is that correct, not the one of your sister-in-law?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know who lived in that -- who had lived in that other apartment before you entered that apartment?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I made a mistake. I first lived with my brother-in-law on number 11, another floor, and then there was a shell, destroyed it all, and then we moved to number 7. And then that's where we lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But my question remains the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is the third time that such questions have been asked this week. They seem to involve displacement of populations. There is no charge against General Galic which involves displacement of population, and they are questions, in my respectful submission, which lack any relevance to the charges which General Galic is facing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly, Mr. President. Now, the Prosecution spent some time explaining or asking the witness whether he had been driven away from Pale, when he arrived in Sarajevo, and so on. So if there was -- on one side, there was will to do this; now the Defence side is trying to find out what happened in Sarajevo itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I strongly dispute that, and I invite my friend to take the Trial Chamber to a transcript reference where I "spent some time explaining or asking the witness whether he had been driven away from Pale." The witness raised the issue; I immediately moved on to a relevant topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I remind you of what is in the transcript of yesterday. The question was: "During the conflict in Sarajevo, were you living in Sarajevo?" The answer then was: "No, at Pale." "Sorry, when did you move from Pale?" "On the 3rd or 4th of July, 1992, they moved us." And then the questioning continued thereafter: "Did you live in Sarajevo?" I do not see any specific questioning in the direction of Pale, and only when the witness indicated that he -- at the beginning of the conflict he lived in Pale. So I do not see that there's any ground in that. But if there's any other relevant aspect, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to confer for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will continue simply with another line of questioning, Mr. President. Thank you. May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if there is any relevance in your question, apart from that you do the same as you, in my view wrongly, suggested the Prosecution did, I'd like to know because this issue might come up again and again. I mean, what's the relevance of if you want to know whether the witness has been --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which was not his, okay, fine, it might have some relevance. If you find it of any importance, please tell us why. And I'm quite willing to allow you to put the questions. But I'd like to know exactly what, apart from whether the Prosecution paid some attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well, Mr. President. But it is a little complex to explain, but I will do it. One of the submissions of the Prosecution is to say there was a policy of terrorising, and what the Defence is trying to submit, as far as it can, is that there was a policy of terror in the other direction which made people leave their place of residence, Serbia. It made Serbs leave their place of residence. Now, if the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you want to establish now is whether there were any empty houses by people that might have left the apartment. So if that's what you -- I'll assist you. Mr. Kadric, the apartment in which you finally lived after the shelling, did you it belong to you or your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know to whom it belonged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know his name. I used to, but I don't know any more. He worked in Union Invest or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know anything about whether it has belonged to a citizen of Serbian origin who might have fled Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that what you wanted to find out, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Three questions are quite enough. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I do not know. I can continue, but perhaps this is now time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much for assisting me. I forgot to look at the clock. Mr. Kadric, we'll first have a break, and then we'll continue. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for giving me the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, good morning once again. You told us a while ago that as the army driver or the soldier, you drove a civilian vehicle, and I believe it was -- you said it was an Opel Corsa. Is that indeed what you said some time ago?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. What or -- what or whom did you drive in that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after shelling, we would be carrying the wounded, the dead, and it was all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, your only duty was to evacuate the wounded in this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody, everybody, not only to evacuate the wounded or civilians or somebody who dies. There were Serbs who had died, and I'd put them in that vehicle and take them to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But this vehicle served for nothing else but for the evacuation of the wounded?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if a civilian had to go to the city, to the hospital or whatever, then this vehicle was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, was this vehicle used also to transport the military?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Therefore, you were the only military person in that vehicle, is that it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did anyone else drive it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you told us yesterday - I did not check the place but I can do it - that you had also another truck, and I believe you said that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it was a livestock truck, a truck to transport the livestock or something that could be used for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but -- there were those two trucks, but they stayed behind in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm reading your answer in the transcript, yet you tell us that those two trucks stayed behind at Lukavica, is that it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At Kula, at the abattoir, at the slaughterhouse, where the prison was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you speak about these two trucks, is it the two trucks that your company had, that you had in your company?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, for the livestock.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, so you had three trucks all in all, is that it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for this answer, and now I'd like to ask you my last questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But for that we need the map, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The question is: You said that the soldiers who were in the area in which you lived had weapons. Did they fire from those arms?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those weapons were there and those weapons were kept at the guard posts. They were never taken anywhere from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, so these -- these weapons were never used throughout the war; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were used, but they were used at those places where the guard posts were, where we kept guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when I say that they were not used, it means that fire was never opened from these weapons for the duration of the time period -- of the time that you knew about them.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Fire was opened from them but only -- I mean so -- only so as to let them know that we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said during your testimony that at a certain time, you were engaged with what, in the transcript, and as far as I remember, was called the TO, which is the Territorial Defence, T-capital O-capital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is. When I came to the TO, that was all there was. There was nothing else there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know the difference between the army, between an army and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what the difference is. The Territorial Defence is -- I mean they guard, they protect the -- their territory, the local area where they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would it be correct to say that the Territorial Defence is organised along military lines?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That is what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. And therefore, it also has brigades, battalions and so on and so forth, doesn't it? The Territorial Defence has it all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not the case there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did the Territorial Defence have its own materiel?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, by "materiel," by "resources," I mean both mechanical -- mechanical devices and weapons.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the weapons that we found in Serb flats, and that is what we were left with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, isn't it true, to your knowledge, that the Territorial Defence had in its headquarters arsenals?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if I understand you well, you are saying that the Territorial Defence had no weapons in their premises? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe the time has now come to show the witness the photo of 360 degrees which was shown him some time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the technical booth assist us -- no, it's the -- no, no. It's the case manager of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Mr. President, if everybody here has the image on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you see it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not. But I see on a lot of screens around me that... [Interpretation] Continue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I think that you can see it on your screen, can you?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you have the image, very good. I believe that it is the same image and that we now see pedestrian crossing and the traffic lights. Is that so? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you please take out the pointer which you perhaps have and tell us where, very exactly, was the point for which the shots came from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, a pointer on a television screen is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I was -- wanted -- under your control and for the transcript, I wanted to describe what the witness is -- would be doing.
