utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So will you, Witness, please continue. Will you please show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin -- Mr. Ierace. I'm even getting confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, obviously the course that is proposed by Mr. Piletta-Zanin will not work if we are not able to see where he places the pointer. Could I respectfully suggest that if he wishes to continue with this course, then perhaps Ms. Pilipovic and I could approach the screen of the witness to see where he points and then one of us could describe, for the benefit of the transcript, where he points to. The only alternative to that would be for the witness to describe from the image --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it will be an excellent exercise, because the parties will come closer to each other, which I very much like. Ms. Pilipovic -- one of the problems is that Ms. Pilipovic will not be able, just as you'll not be able any more, to hear what is said. So although the thought is very attractive for me, for practical reasons it might not work out. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you please guide the witness such that we'll always have a clear description of what he -- there are two additional headphones there. You can also choose the channel, I suggest? Yes. So if you dare to come that close to each other, Ms. Pilipovic, and then use the headphones. So everyone has the right channel on his -- yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So now we shall try to be precise with the help of both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, will you please show -- will you please point here -- will you please be so kind, to the best of your recollection, as to point at the place from which the fire came from, which the fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, if you can do that, will you please point at it slowly so that you can describe precisely which is the building from which the fire was opened. Witness, is it the building which is immediately behind the traffic lights and where we see two trees? Is that the building that we see here? So for the transcript, it is the building in the centre of the photograph behind the traffic lights and with two trees situated along the facade of the building. Would that be correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is nodding no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, where exactly is the building from which the fire could have been opened? Can you please place it.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, can you describe it? I see you are pointing to your right. Can you describe the building that you are referring to? Does it mean the building which is in the rear and which is on the right-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is our building. These are our buildings, and these are these smaller buildings, that home for the blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Right. Now, Witness, is it the building which is behind this grey box which looks like an industrial box on the pavement?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that box was not there. There was nothing like it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage I can provide a description as to where the witness indicated the source of fire in response to the second-last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the Defence does not object. It is quite to the contrary because we do not know exactly to where the witness is pointing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the image on the screen at the moment shows a pedestrian crossing in the bottom centre. The blue garbage bin is to the right of the image. The position indicated by the witness was to the right of the blue garbage bin; that is, in between the high-rise, the end of the high-rise buildings to the left, and the tree to the right. In that space, which is approximately a centimetre wide on the image, there appears a blue portion beneath it, a reddish portion, and a bit of a shadow beneath it. About a centimetre below is the grass. The witness pointed to the reddish portion which occupies the space between the green tree to the right and the last of the high-rise buildings to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I see a mouse which is moving over the screen. Can the case manager please point the mouse towards this place which is shown by -- which is pointed at by the witness. Is that possible? Can the mouse be used for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it possible to move this marker without changing the picture? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perfect, excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you now see a sign? It is next to a tree. Is that the place that you indicated?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we continue in this way? Would this be a good kind of cooperation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's then necessary to describe in words, but clarification can be made by putting the pointer at the specific point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm talking to the case manager. Can you please put the cursor on the building which was indicated by the witness and as indicated by Mr. Ierace? That is -- this is the high-rise building which is on the right-hand side -- on the left-hand side of the image, a little bit to -- no, no, no, between two trees, between the two trees. Will you come back more? More. More. To the right, to the right, go to the right of the image. Go back where you were before. Yes, you were in a perfect place. Yes, excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you see the cursor. You said a moment ago that there was a hole which was made in the facade of the building from which fire was opened. Can you tell us where exactly was that hole? Can we see it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you can't. I can't even see the building here but the hole was on the first floor, not on the ground floor. It was on the first floor near to the street. The street was the straight one which goes between the -- those trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, may we return to the bar tables?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the counsel. Can you please come closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might we return to the bar tables at this stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You want to go back to your original positions. I have full understanding for that. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And thank you, Mr. Ierace, and thank you, case manager, for the assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I believe I heard you say a moment ago that on this photograph, you could not see the place from which the fire was opened. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Right, yes, yes, yes, on this photograph. I understand. One cannot see it on this photograph. Is that how I should understand your words?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less. You can see something white and something red.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel and witness please break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the interpreters still have problems in following. Would you please slow down. And also, may I ask Mr. Kadric to wait until -- you have a picture on your screen now. That's very difficult to know exactly where the text would have stopped moving. But could you please take a break every time between the question, once it's put to you, and the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much for your comments, Mr. President. I'm very sorry. I'll slow down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, we shall now ask that this image be panned to the right and I will ask you, when you think that you are able to locate precisely the place, the spot, from which the fire came, to then tell us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the image -- can this be panned, please, to the right? In the other direction. Yes, perfect. Can we stop now, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, and from this angle here, can you see the place from which the shots came precisely?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the two buildings here and the one to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: May we approach the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sorry, Witness, I will ask you to slowly and precisely point from where, according to your recollection, came those shots. And Ms. Counsel Pilipovic will indicate it into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is this point here and the roof.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness is pointing at two white dots, above which one can see at a distance a roof.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not a roof, no. This is not a roof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, could you please guide the case manager of the Prosecutor's Office to indicate with the marker on the screen exactly, so you say "down" or "left" or "right," so until the marker is exactly at the spot which you indicated. Would it be down to start with or ... Could you please guide, just say "down" or "right" or "left."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Down, to the left, to the left, to the left, yes, left, here, left, left, more to the left, more to the left, and more to the left, and more to the left, and more to the left, more to the left. Stop. Now a bit to the right, to the right, a bit more to the right, lower down, a little bit down, to the left. There. About that. But this is a photograph, so you can't be quite exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, thank you for this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for the transcript, the cursor is practically at the bottom of the building, which is the last building in the second row of buildings on the screen and quite near a tree line, and that is dark green, and to the left, there is the first cluster of trees in the foreground. I believe that for the transcript, Mr. President, this will be objective enough. Thank you, Witness. I would like to continue on this photograph but we no longer need our assistants, to whom I extend my thanks. Now, Madam Case Manager, could you continue the rotation, please. Still to the right, please. Could we perhaps stop. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, under the cursor that you can see in the centre of the image, there is an area which seems to be made up of buildings that are of medium height. Could you tell us what they are? What is this area?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stupsko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, this hill, under whose control was it in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I say? How can I say it? Serbian army, Serb army, they kept it there while the Oslobodjenja building was the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say, "liberation forces," you mean there were two forces on this hill?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I meant Oslobodjenja printing house, the building, Oslobodjenja building. This was the journalists. That had burnt from that hill. It was -- they fired shots which set it on fire and it was burning for days, and that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, who was in the Oslobodjenja building, which is a printing house?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a printing house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. We agree that this was a printing house. But could you tell us who was in control of that building?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps -- THE COURT: Yes, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My friend just changed the question so I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm going to reread the question in the transcript so that I can be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to know who was in -- who was controlling the Oslobodjenja building that question has been answered already, hasn't it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? The witness said, "How can I say it?" He was referring to the Stupsko Brdo. He said, "How could I say it? Serbian army, Serb army, they kept it there, while this --" and then he referred to the Oslobodjenja building -- "was the other side." So unless you find more than two parties in the conflict, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But there were many sides unfortunately. There was the Serb army, which was there near Stup so I'm not sure whether it is efficient but if it is clear to the Chamber, then all the better, of course. I thought it would be useful to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did I understand you well, Mr. Kadric, that the Oslobodjenja building was under the control of the Bosnian -- Bosnia-Herzegovina side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: There was no presence of a Croat army in the building?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know if a Croat army was anywhere near this area?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the other area, further down from Stup.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you to continue to rotate the image, please. Perhaps we could stop here, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you indicate, could you tell us the name of the hill that we can see -- that we can see behind this Bulevar which goes on into the background?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Buljakov Potok. I don't know what the hill is called. But this is Buljakov Potok and also a rubbish dump. To the right is a rubbish dump, but that is Buljakovo settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, do you know under whose control in a military sense still was of that area?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that we are finished with the photograph. We would now like to show a map to the witness, if the Chamber will allow it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This is a map that you have already seen, and we have tried to erase all the markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you asked for all markings to be erased, but I'm not sure whether we managed to have it done. I don't know whether everyone has a map. I think -- I believe they do. Now, could we have the -- can we see the map on the screen, please. Here we are. I believe everyone can see the map now. Mr. President, may I continue? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have on your right -- yes, very well. Yes, look towards your right, and you have a map before you which you can also see on your screen. And could you please take your time, and if you can tell us if you can recognise this partial map of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Thank you. Would it be possible, Witness, to indicate for us the area of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you indicate with a pointer on the area of Nedzarici, please?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately. I'm not totally accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, would it be possible to ask that the witness be given a black marker pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please give a black marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you now make a circle around the area that you have just indicated on this map.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Could you perhaps put a number "1" inside this area so that we know that this area indicates the Nedzarici area.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Perhaps next to, next to the area. That's it. No, no, no. Not inside; next to it.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Witness, could you please indicate where one or several command posts were that we spoke about earlier in relation to your military duty.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you perhaps make a cross, perhaps a slightly more visible cross, please.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps you could mark a number "2" next to it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, near this area, was there an area where there were Civilian Defence premises near there, or perhaps the premises of the Territorial Defence anywhere near this area? And if your answer is yes, then please tell me so.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please mark a number "3" next to this dot.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Still on the right of the dot.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. This is the road, so it's further down. So it's roughly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, for the transcript, the witness changed his first dot, and his new point is in the vertical axe which goes up from number 1 and it goes in the upper part above number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you perhaps put a number "3" next to the point. If you put it on top of the old dot -- yes -- then we can see it clearly. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, where did you live at the time? Can you indicate it for us on the map?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in number 7. Here. There was the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, for the transcript, the witness is indicating the cross next to number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, thank you very much, Witness. Now, we'll go to the neighbourhood that you mentioned yourself, which is the neighbourhood of Dobrinja. And I believe, as far as I can recall, you said that the HQ of the 5th Motorised Brigade was in Dobrinja, and I believe that you said Dobrinja II. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Now, Witness, the map that you can see before you, could you tell us where Dobrinja is on it, and more precisely, Dobrinja II, and if you can put number 2 in Roman numerals, please.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately here. Let me just see where the water is. The river is -- yes, the river is line. I would say that this is where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. On the river.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please make a marking of a Roman numeral number 2 to the area which corresponds to Dobrinja II, that is, two parallel lines, please. If you prefer, you can just put a number "4" next to it, but this is just so that we don't have any confusion later on. Witness, the area that you indicated a moment ago, I believe that you said that that was Dobrinja II. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is where I will say where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please mark a number "4." It will be simpler.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you tell us exactly in Dobrinja II where the premises of the 5th Motorised Brigade were?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was approximately here where the number 4 is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please give us the street again, which was not translated for the transcript? You did say -- could you give us the name of the street, please.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, as far as you know, in Dobrinja, were there other military installations, military facilities, that had command posts there?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I only came there. I wasn't always there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you indicated that the vehicle that you were driving at the time was used to transport the wounded. Did you also take them to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know, in your capacity as a soldier, how many battalions were there in the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About four.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was their strength? I think you said it already, but perhaps you can give us again the total strength of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Very last question: Sir, did your son go to school during --

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was his school and where was it?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went to the -- to one, and then when he returned from the Emirates, he then went to the economics school up in town. I think it was in Dzure Dzakovica Street. That's where his school was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. Did he go every day?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was possible, he did go every day. When there was shooting, he did not go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you show us on the map where this school was? Could you indicate for us on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see it on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Does this mean that this is much further away from Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How often did your son go to school?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went, but I don't know exactly when he did go and when he didn't go. This all changed, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But he did go to school, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. But I don't know when he went and when he didn't go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You were not aware of the rhythm that he followed to go to school?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember when it was, how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Your son -- your son lived with you in your apartment, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did your son finish his school, complete his school?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He completed about one year or so, and he -- then he was shot, and then he didn't complete. And then when he returned from the Emirates, he then continued with his schooling.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But before he was wounded, was he able to finish his previous year in the college?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean to complete?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That is, to go to the end of the school year, to the end of the school year of the year in question.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he was wounded, he was not able to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question was about the period preceding the wounded.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably went, but I don't know what you're trying to get out of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The truth, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're looking for the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Mr. President, arising out of the last few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that your son did not go to school when there was shooting?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I forgot how often he went. But of course, if there was a lot of shooting, when there was shelling, when it was practically thundering all day, of course I wouldn't allow him to go to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Judge Nieto-Navia will put some questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please put the photograph 3277-4301. Do you see in the middle of the photo to the left of the centre, two blue lines drawn by you?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: And what are those lines? What do they indicate?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the trees were lower. What I mean is the trees were lower then than it was when the picture was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: That's what the lines signify.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was asked the question if the trees were higher or lower, and I put a line there to cut off how high, so that's what I marked. Of course, they were lower because seven or eight years had passed since the shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, since Judge El Mahdi nor myself have any additional questions to you, this is the conclusion of your examination as a witness. We are all aware of that very long way you came from Sarajevo to The Hague, and we would like to thank you very much for taking the effort to come such a -- from such a far distance. You well understand that it's of great importance for this Court to hear the answers to questions put by both parties to the witnesses, and also the answers given to questions put to you by the Judges. This information is very important for us since we'll have to take decisions and we are dependent on the information that is brought into this courtroom, and since you have contributed to that, we would like to thank you very much. And of course, I wish you a very safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, then, would you please lead Mr. Kadric out of the courtroom? Thank you, Mr. Kadric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before the next witness is brought in, could I say a few words at this point about the issue raised by Mr. Piletta-Zanin this morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shall we first deal with the exhibits and then -- I should say documents, because they are not exhibits yet. Madam Registrar, if you could please assist me, as far as I can see, the following documents have been tendered in evidence. First is P3108, which is a map, a premarked map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the second, as far as I can see, is P3107, which is a sketch of a vehicle. If it would assist you, it looks approximately like this. You find it, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I found it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has been additionally marked during the -- it has been marked during the examination. Then we have P3280N, which is, am I correct in my understanding, the video?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we have P3279N, which is the 360-degree photographs on the CD-ROM.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have P3277, which is a premarked photograph. That's the photograph that has just been shown to the witness, as far as I understand. That's the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a set of two photos under one number. That's P3279NN. Then we finally have a Defence Exhibit, which is a map which has not been numbered yet, but it will then get the next number on the exhibit list. Could you please tell us what would be the next number on the Defence exhibit list. I think we are approximately in our mid-40s.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Defence D48, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 48. They are all admitted into evidence. Please, Mr. Ierace, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this morning, Mr. Piletta-Zanin said that the Defence had been given some documents by the Prosecution, but he said that the documents were exhibits, and they were given to the Defence yesterday for a crucial witness that the Prosecution is calling next week. I have made some inquiries. The documents are not exhibits. They are not proposed exhibits. The witness will not be called next week, will not be called indeed for three or four weeks. The photographs, which were entirely illegible, were attached to a statement by [redacted] which was served on the Defence as part of our disclosure obligations. [redacted] [redacted] is a witness who will be called in the shelling phase. I anticipate he will not be called for three or four weeks. The photographs come from a report which was attached to the statement served yesterday. The statement entirely concerns events after the tenure of General Galic. In other words, there is nothing in the statement or the attached report which will be relied upon for the Prosecution. The only reason it was served was as part of our disclosure obligations. In any event, I will ascertain as to whether we have photographs which are legible, and if we do, either copies will be provided to the Defence or they will be given an opportunity to inspect them. I suspect that, given the entirely useless nature of the photocopies provided to the Defence, that the originals are either no better or only slightly better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I just first ask you a question: What made you believe that these documents would be tendered as exhibits next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I shall be very precise. I do not know if I said next week or following -- one of the following weeks, but I do not know. I can check it in the transcript. But it is for one of the forthcoming witnesses, at any rate. It is one of the forthcoming witnesses. And we think that there are -- that there is a considerable chance that these documents will be tendered, and if we want to conscientiously look at the things, and if we make the trouble to go through them, then we can do that only with legible documents. And for a document to be usable, that is not the way in which they were given us. And that is the only reason I raised it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, allow me, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to assist you in finding in the transcript exactly what you said. It's on page 1, lines 15 and following. "Documents given by the Prosecution because there is a number of exhibits that we were given yesterday for crucial witness that we should hear next week." That's what you said. That's what you told the Court. Would you please tell me on what basis you informed the Court that it was about a witness which would appear next week, since there seems to be some dispute on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly it was a misreading. It was our impression, but if that was not the case, in that case, I apologise, but we understood that this witness would be coming the next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What gave you reason to assume that, since we have a list of witnesses for next week, haven't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. No. I think it was simply a case much misreading. I received this information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you received these documents yesterday, and if you're not happy with them, would you perhaps pay more attention to the first thing you told the Court, that you are better communicating with the Prosecution. There was no reason whatsoever not to find out between the two parties this morning what was the function of these documents, whether the Prosecution could provide you with any better copies, and when they would be used in evidence, instead of telling us that it would be next week. As I urged before, it's first up to the parties to communicate to each other, and only if you cannot solve your problems, then ask the intervention of the bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will bear this in mind. We shall check it, but at least the document remains illegible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everything has been said about this, what has to be said. Mr. Ierace, would you please call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I call Medina Omerovic. And I can indicate that her evidence relates to schedule -- sniping incident number 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in this courtroom, Ms. Omerovic. Prior to giving testimony in this courtroom, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text will be given to you now by the usher, and I invite to you make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Omerovic. Please be seated. Ms. Omerovic, since you have been called as a witness for the Prosecution, you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is your name Medina Omerovic?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you born on the 17th of October, 1977?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In 1992, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When the armed conflict began around the middle of 1992, whereabouts were you living? What address?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Dure Jaksica 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was that place? Was it a house or an apartment block or something else?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: An apartment block.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, at some stage during the conflict, did you have a friend by the name of Sanela Muratovic?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was she younger than you or older than you or about the same age?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: She was younger than I.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How much younger than you was she?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: About a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there a time during the conflict that you were with your friend and she was shot?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the date that that happened?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: The 26th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what street were you and she when she was shot?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: In Dure Jaksica 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you said earlier that was the street and the number where you lived. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you headed towards your place of residence or away from your place of residence or what at the time that she was shot?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: We were walking towards the building that I lived in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your date of birth, on that date, were you age 16?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you coming from at the time that she was shot? Where had you been?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: We had been to see my sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And why were you going back towards your place?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: We were going there to get a book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And where exactly were you when she was shot? By that, I mean were you on some grass somewhere or on a footpath or whereabouts? What type of surface?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: It was a street, and we had started crossing it towards my building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you had been living in that building since the beginning of the war. Whereabouts was the nearest part of the confrontation line from your building, approximately how far from your building?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Not far. There was only a street between us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And had there been some measures taken by this date, the date that your friend was shot, to make the area safer for civilians such as yourselves to cross the street?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were warned by soldiers who were on the other side that sniper fire had started and to hurry up. And so we started running, and then it happened at that very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you ran across the road, whereabouts was the confrontation line? Was it to your left or to your right or straight ahead or behind you?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was in front and to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As the two of you ran across the road, where was Sanela in relation to you, in particular at the instant she was shot? Was she to your left, or to your right, or somewhere else; behind, in front?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: To my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened as you and she ran across the road.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: We heard a shot. We started running, and I saw that Sanela had been hit because there was blood on her T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Go on. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Then we went down into a trench and soldiers ran up to us and took her to a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that you were heading back to your place in order to get a book. Was there any other danger area that you had to cross on your journey back to your apartment, apart from the street outside your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: There were quite a number of danger spots, but they were rather well protected. There was some large containers so that we were relatively safe when going there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you still know Sanela Muratovic?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to work out why there was blood on her T-shirt?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Because she was hit, because a bullet struck her. She was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see the wound at some stage, either that day or at a later time? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to -- withdraw that. Whereabouts on her T-shirt was the blood that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: On her right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether it was towards the front of her right shoulder or towards the back or the side or in more than one place?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Front, on the front side of her right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would take it a bit more... Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was Sanela wearing at that time that she was shot, apart from her T-shirt?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: She was wearing trousers and sneakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were you wearing?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I had shorts, a T-shirt, and sneakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown the video which is P3280O.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think we have still got seven minutes, so it's useful to play the video, and then you have time to put a few questions to the witness. So please proceed, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, you've told us that you lived in this apartment building through the conflict. There was an area of danger immediately out of -- at the front of the apartment block. And by the time this happened in mid-1994, you were 16. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you know other children, apart from your friend Sanela, who lived in that same area during those years?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your answers, it would seem that you lived in an area of constant and extreme danger; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you live all of the time -- I withdraw that. The apartment in which you lived was on what floor of the block?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: The third floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any period of time that you lived at that address, but not on the third floor?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where was that in the building?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: In the cellar of the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For how long did you live in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: For a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many times did you come out of the cellar in that one-year period?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Not once.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you live in the cellar with your family?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there any other families that lived in the cellar with you?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Seven families, including ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did any of those other families include children?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any power when you were living in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: There was in the beginning, but later on, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did that one year of your life commence?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: In April, 1992. Could have been late April.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the cellar have any windows? And if so, how many?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: One small.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With your hands, could you show us the size of the window?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was one of the boys, one of the children who spent that year with you in the cellar Dejan Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, just for the sake of the record, the witness has indicated the size of the window. I think she indicated a size of approximately 20 by 40 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: In the spring of 1994, he was killed. He went out into the street - it happened in the same street but a bit further away, and on the other side - and a sniper got him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How do you know that he was killed in that spot?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Well, first I had heard the noise and then we went to the window, even though it was dangerous, and we saw him lying down in the street, and his dad then went out and he died shortly afterwards. I mean, he could have lived for another ten seconds or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Omerovic, we will first have a break, and then Mr. Ierace will continue examining you. So we will adjourn until ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might we view the video which is P3280O.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, would you please look at the computer screen in front of you and we should shortly see a video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please show me, as closely as you can recall, where the edges of the trench were at around the time when your friend Sanela Muratovic was shot? I'll mark this plane with yellow paint. I'll mark this plane with yellow paint. Could you please point in the direction in which you and Sanela were travelling that day at the time when Sanela was shot, to the best of your recollection. Would you please show me approximately, to the best of your recollection, where you were at the time that Sanela was shot. And in relation to yourself, can you indicate, please, approximately where, to the best of your recollection, Sanela was located."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, did you recognise yourself on that video?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The investigator asked you to point out certain things. When you complied with his requests, did you do so truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The first request that he made was for you to indicate a position of a trench. And you indicated, I think, two sides of the trench, and you did so alongside a footpath curb. Did that trench completely cross the road from that curb?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You indicated that you and Sanela were in a position to the right of that trench at the time that she was shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It seems from the video that you and she had only just left the curb at the moment that she was shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, over the period of the armed conflict that you were not in the cellar, did you develop an understanding as to the source or sources of fire in relation to the area outside your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were those -- where was that source or sources of fire?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: There was the institute for blind children, and also the surrounding area of Nedzarici behind our building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3279OO. It's an exhibit which comprises two photographs. I ask the photograph which ends with the numbers "08" be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, will you please turn to your right and look at the photograph which is placed on the white board. Do you recognise what appears in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is that area?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: This is the locality of Nedzarici. It was -- the photograph was taken in front of the institute for blind children.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the confrontation line between the opposing forces at the time that Sanela was shot? And in particular, can you see on that photograph where the confrontation line was or not?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the desk in front of you, there is a metal pointer. Could you take that and point to the position of the front line at that time on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has drawn the pointer across the photograph from left to right, commencing at what appears to be a concrete shell of a building on the lower left, drawing the pointer across towards the bottom of the line of high-rise apartments which appear on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, in relation to the high-rise buildings which appear about halfway down the photograph and to the right of centre, do you agree that in this photograph they appear to be in a semi-demolished condition?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where was the front line at that place in relation to those buildings? In other words, were those buildings on the front line, or were they slightly either side of the front line, on one side of the front line?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: On the other side, on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "on the other side," do you understand the opposing forces to be the Bosnian Serb army and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On which side were those buildings?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Which buildings do you mean? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you see that on the right-hand side of the photograph, there are the buildings which appear to be semi-derelict, if I could put it that way?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you just point to those buildings with your pointer so that we all make sure we understand what we're talking about. Because when you do that, we can see on our screens where you are pointing.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you do it once more, please.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Could you place your pointer on the -- what appears to be the concrete building on the left-hand side of the photograph, and it appears to be just a ground floor. Could you place your pointer on that building.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just a little lower. Could you bring the tip of your pointer down a little lower. A bit lower further.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, that building that you're pointing to at the moment, which side of the confrontation line was that on, or was it in the middle of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: It was in the middle of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you point to the tree which appears in the middle of the photograph approximately.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, would you move your pointer slightly to the right of the tree. Further to the right. A little further up.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, that line of buildings, that is the buildings which extend from the tree to the edge of the photograph on the right-hand side, whereabouts were those buildings in relation to the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On which side of the confrontation line? In other words, the Bosnian Serb Army side or the side where you lived?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: On the side that I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was anyone living in those buildings in 1994, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you know anyone who lived in those buildings?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: A few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, towards the centre of the photograph, just to the left of the tree, there appears the side of a building which is reddish-brown and it has white, horizontal stripes. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please point to it and hold the pointer there for a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Beneath that, at ground level, there appears a white building of just one storey, that is the ground level, with a series of windows. Could you please point to that.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. What is that building, that is the white building which is just a ground-level construction?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: That is a restaurant, which at the time was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now look at the second photograph. And perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO. It ends with the numbers 17A. Do you recognise this photograph to be --

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And by comparing it to the earlier photograph, does it appear to be a telephoto shot of the area in the centre of the previous photograph?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given that, is the white building in this photograph, that is ending with 17A, the cafe that you referred to -- the restaurant, rather, that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In this photograph, one can see damage to the buildings except for the restaurant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the white building to the right, with the balconies, one can see what appear to be black spots on the wall; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the wall of the red brick building, above the restaurant, one can also see what appear to be small holes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know what caused those holes?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: This is from shelling and from sniping.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Between those two buildings, in the background, one can see some balconies with damage to the walls of that building. Can you see that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that damage have the same cause?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness now be shown Exhibit P3270, which also consists of two photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I just ask you one question? The first exhibit, P3280, the video, you added a single O. For 3279, you added the double O. Is there any specific reason for that? Otherwise, I can imagine it would create some confusion, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you will answer the question later, if it has to be found out. You continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the photograph which does not have the pen markings on it be placed on the ELMO. For the record, this is part of Exhibit P3270.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the view which appears in the photograph before you?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that photograph show the cafe that -- the restaurant that you've earlier referred to?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In this photograph, it has an awning extended; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Also in this photograph, we can see more of the buildings between the red brick building on the left and the white building with the balconies on the right; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The buildings in the middle have damage to their fronts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please now look at the second photograph in that exhibit. Do you recognise on that photograph your signature and the date 26 September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you place cross-hatching on the restaurant to indicate that it was not there at the time of this incident?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please explain the significance of the cross-hatching.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: The restaurant did not exist at the time of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness now be shown the 360-degree photograph, which, Mr. President, I have as P3279O. Perhaps the witness's screen could be switched to Computer Evidence. Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your earlier evidence, is that the restaurant on the screen now which --

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- was not -- all right. And that's the restaurant that was not there at the time of the incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I notice that there is some distortion of the image on the computer screen, which does not appear on the screen attached to the computer playing it. For the moment, I don't think it's of any significance, but I simply draw it to the Chamber's attention. Could the image please be moved slowly to the right? Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, I'd like you to accept from me that this photograph was taken from the spot you indicated to the investigator Sanela was at when she was shot. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you watch this image on your screen, if you see either the school for the blind or the direction in which it was, could you please say so.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please keep moving the image to the right. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see in the photograph, at the moment, the apartment building in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it the building slightly to the right of centre, that is, a light-brown colour with white horizontal stripes?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which is the part of the building that you were running towards with Sanela on the 26th of June, 1994? Could you describe it to us in words?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: This is the back entrance. In fact, it's not a real entrance, but we had to go through that entrance, through that cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is the cellar door visible on the photograph at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it obscured by some bushes or grass?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How far along the side of that building is it? In other words, is it towards the middle or towards the left or the right?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right, I'll come back to that. Do you see there's a line of windows running down the building?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you can imagine that line being extended down to ground level, would it be to the left of that line or to the right of that line or immediately under those windows?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the road surface, one can see two lines. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where was the trench in relation to those two lines?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Between the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right. All right. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think we've now gone right around. At any stage did you see the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you see it in the image which is on the screen now, or is it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it faster to go to the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please tell us when you see it.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Now I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Can you describe its position in relation to the portion of your apartment block that we can see to the left of the picture. Could you describe in words where it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if my friend has no objection to leading, perhaps I could give that description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have absolutely no objection, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see that firstly part of your -- withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please pan the picture further to the left. Stop. And zoom in. Further. Further. Further. Further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid that we are now in a picture of the earlier incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... familiar to me. That's not an urban area we see now. I notice that we had several time difficulties whenever we zoom in too much. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, we have a close-up of the edge, that is the right-sided edge, of the building in which you lived which is coloured light-brown with white horizontal stripes. Immediately to the right of the apartment as one looks at the image, there is firstly some foliage, and then, beyond that, what appear to be some buildings. And above the buildings, one can see a corner of a building painted white with what appears to be a window and a dark-coloured gabled roof. Do you see that building?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is that building?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: This is the institute for blind children.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you told us this morning before the break that following you hearing a noise when you were in your apartment, you went to the window and saw Dejan Stevanovic lying in the street. From where he was lying, was it possible to see the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it possible to see any other parts of territory which were on the Bosnian Serbian side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which were those parts? Could you describe them?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: More to the right, there were houses, buildings, on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the right of where?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: From my building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, at this stage, might the witness be shown Exhibit P3098. That is a map. If the left side of that map could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, firstly, on that map, do you see your signature and a date?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is the date the 8th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Going back to the left side of the map, did you place some marks in red ink on that map, on that date?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you point to a marking in red ink which shows a cross and the letter "A" alongside it, with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you mean to indicate by that mark?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: The spot where Sanela was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you also place a mark with -- that is, a cross with a number "1" alongside it on the map?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you point to that mark.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you mean to indicate by it?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: The spot from which the shot came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now please take a blue marker pen that the usher will give you and place a cross on the spot where you saw Dejan Stevanovic lying after he was shot, at the time he was shot.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you firstly indicate with the pointer the areas on the Bosnian Serb Army of the confrontation line that were visible from that spot.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you've just, with the pointer, indicated an arc; is that correct? I'll rephrase the question. You've placed a blue cross on the map to indicate where Dejan Stevanovic was observed by you to be after you heard the noise; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given your familiarity with the area, if you were to stand on the spot where you saw him lying on the ground, what areas on the Bosnian Serb Army side of the confrontation line could you actually see from that spot? Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. More particularly, are you able to see those areas on the map? And please take your time.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Will you take the blue marker pen and draw a line around that area that you've just indicated.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you could just stop there for a moment. I think earlier you said that it wasn't possible to see the school for the blind from the spot where Dejan Stevanovic was shot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you just drawn the line through the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, I'm not particularly good with maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
