utterances.text: All right. Earlier, I asked you to indicate the part of the Bosnian Serb Army side of the confrontation line that you could see from where Dejan Stevanovic was shot. Do you remember that? Do you remember I asked you that question?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do you remember that you pointed to an area just to the right of the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do you remember that, before I showed you the map, you said that the area was, I think, further to the right of your apartment block?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Could you take the pen and draw a circle around that area that you pointed to earlier, that is the part on the Bosnian Serb Army side that you could see from where Dejan Stevanovic was shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, if you have difficulties doing it on the map, please tell us, since you told us before that you had some -- you are not very good at maps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true. I don't find my way around them easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you a question in between? Ms. Omerovic, you told us that you could not see -- that from the place where Dejan Stevanovic was -- where you saw him lying, you could not see from that spot the school for the blind. When you gave this answer, did you intend to say that from the place where you were when you saw him lying down - and as far as I understood, that was in the cellar behind the window - that you could not see from that place the school for the blind? Or that from the place where you saw Dejan Stevanovic lying - so if you would be at that spot - that you could not see the school for the blind from there? So was it that you could not see it from the cellar or was it that you would not be able to see it from the spot where Dejan Stevanovic was lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the spot where he was lying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From there, you could not see the school of the blind, if you would be at that same spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just to clarify something coming out of that question by the President, where were you -- I'll withdraw that. You told us earlier that you spent a year in the cellar starting from April 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And you also said that this incident happened, the incident when Dejan Stevanovic was shot, happened in the spring of 1994. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you when you heard the noise and went to the window? Were you in the cellar or were you somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: In my flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what floor was that on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise for misquoting. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What floor was it on? I'm sorry, I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: In my flat on the third floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And as you look out of your window on the third floor, was it possible from that window to see the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. If you imagine standing on the spot where you saw Dejan Stevanovic lying on the road, from there, could you have seen the school for the blind, do you think?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is all right, Your Honour. The witness has already answered that from the place, from that place, I could not see it. And my learned friend repeated the question, but the witness confirmed her answer so it is all right. And that was my objection, that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it was asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. I would have sustained the objection, but the question has been answered. And it doesn't make any change at this moment. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, just to clarify your evidence, do I understand you to be saying that if you stood on the spot where Dejan Stevanovic was shot, you could see an area on the Bosnian Serb army side of the confrontation which was to the right of the school for the blind. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic, we've still got 5 minutes to go. Would there be an area you could touch upon which could be finished in 5 minutes approximately, since we have to leave the courtroom at quarter past [sic]. I'd like to use the 5 minutes, but perhaps in your selection of items to...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Omerovic, Ms. Pilipovic, who is counsel for the Defence, will now put questions to you. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Omerovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if and when you talked with the Tribunal -- with Tribunal investigators?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: In 1995 or 6. I'm not quite sure. Then in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that you talked with the -- with OTP investigators on the 8th of November, 1995, would be able to tell me if that is correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I don't really remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But if I show you the statement which you signed, would then you recognise it and confirm that it was your statement?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist Ms. Pilipovic in just showing the statement, and especially the signatures on it. Ms. Omerovic, you find your signature on these pages just shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please return it to Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour. Just one question more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also see the 4th of October, 2000, on the statement?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also speak with investigators, too?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Ms. Pilipovic? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This statement carries your signature. Below that, it says the 4th of October, 2000. Can you explain what does this date mean, the 4th of October, 2000? And in the upper part where all the particulars are, it says the 8th of November, 1995. So the date of the interview was the 8th of November, 1995, and what you wrote here was the 4th of October, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you to explain it to me, whether this signature which you have here, did you sign it on the 4th of October, 2000, or did you sign it on the 8th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC
utterances.text: I remember that I signed it on -- in November 1995. But whether on the 4th of October, there was yet another interview, whether I signed something, I just don't know. I simply cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you tell us at the time when you gave your statement on the 8th of November, 1995, bearing in mind that the interview was conducted with you perhaps a year, year and a half after the incident about which you told us today, can you tell us, when was your memory fresher in relation to the time of the incident? Was it fresher in 1995 or today? When did you remember? When did you recall better the events relating to the incident?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is now time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic. Thank you for your assistance. Mr. Usher, would you please bring the statement back to Ms. Pilipovic. I have one final question to Mr. Ierace at this very moment. Mr. Ierace, we have been shown several times the 360-degrees photographs. You guided us how to get the software, how to play them, and you said you can get them from the internet. Since the Tribunal does not allow Judges to download anything from the internet and install it on their computers, the Bench would very much like to have a copy of the software which makes it possible to view these photos. And I would like to hear from the Defence whether they have been able to, not being under the same restrictions as the Bench is, to download the software from the internet. If not, would then please the Prosecution provide them with the software necessary to view the photographs. Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence has managed to obtain these photographs through its own resources so that we don't have a problem. But possibly if technically perhaps we can offer a solution, we shall be very delighted to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There would be no problem for me as well, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to do it at home and bring it to the Tribunal. But since I'm not allowed to install whatever software on my computer here unless it comes from either the OTP or from the Tribunal itself, I'm afraid I have to. But thank you very much for the offered assistance. I'm sure you'll be able to solve this problem for us, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Do you wish for a ten-second explanation in relation to the double O exhibit number at this stage or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although from what I heard later on, I can imagine what it would be, but if it's no problem for someone else, then we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As Your Honour pleases. THE COURT: Yes, please. Ms. Omerovic, your examination has not been finished yet, but since it's Friday today, we will continue after the weekend since this courtroom has to be used this afternoon for another case. So we will continue next Monday in this same courtroom at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. So then the cross-examination will continue. If there is nothing else before the weekend to be brought to my attention, we will adjourn until next Monday at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
